sections.overview: The Peacock Moth is a geometrid recorded in the British Isles and widely across much of France.
sections.identification: It may be confused with the Sharp-angled Peacock or Dusky Peacock, especially when worn.
sections.habitat: French regional accounts associate it with humid broad-leaved woods.
sections.diet: Its caterpillars feed on birches and other deciduous trees, including willow, alder and oak.
sections.behavior: In Poitou-Charentes, adults are recorded in two periods: May–June and August–September.
sections.reproduction: The French regional account reports an overwintering chrysalis.
sections.ecology: The Dusky Peacock, Macaria signaria, is a close lookalike; its British account says it lacks the dark-edged forewing notch seen in the Peacock and Sharp-angled Peacock.
sections.conservation: A regional French species record says it has not been assessed on any Red List; this is not a global conservation assessment.
